$comment: Documented exceptions for the `audit` CI job (scripts/audit-check.mjs).
Every entry MUST carry: an `advisory` (GHSA id) or a `package` scope, a `reason`,
an `approvedBy`, and an `expires` date (YYYY-MM-DD). An entry without `expires`,
or past its `expires` date, does not waive anything AND fails the job — an expired
waiver forces a re-review instead of letting accepted risk become permanent.
Prefer advisory-scoped entries. Package-scoped entries are used below only where a
single upstream version bump resolves a whole cluster of advisories at once, and
enumerating 30+ ids would imply a per-advisory review that did not happen.
Baseline recorded 2026-08-14 during the P0-adapted slice: npm audit reported
14 vulnerabilities (2 low, 11 high, 1 critical) against the dependency set pinned
Updated 2026-08-14 by the dependency-security slice: next 14.2.0 -> 14.2.35,
non-breaking `npm audit fix`. npm audit now reports 7 vulnerabilities
(2 low, 5 high, 0 critical). The critical Next.js middleware authorization bypass
GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw is CLEARED. Nine waivers were deleted because their advisories

exceptions.reason: next is now 14.2.35, the newest release on the 14.2.x line. That bump cleared the critical middleware authorization bypass (GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw) plus four highs (GHSA-gp8f-8m3g-qvj9 cache poisoning, GHSA-7gfc-8cq8-jh5f authorization bypass, GHSA-mwv6-3258-q52c and GHSA-5j59-xgg2-r9c4 RSC DoS). Eight highs remain — GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf, GHSA-q4gf-8mx6-v5v3, GHSA-8h8q-6873-q5fj, GHSA-c4j6-fc7j-m34r, GHSA-36qx-fr4f-26g5, GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj, GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x, GHSA-p9j2-gv94-2wf4. Every one of these is first fixed in the 15.5.x line (npm reports the only fix as next@16.3.1, semver-major), so none can be resolved without leaving Next 14; that migration is deliberately out of scope for this slice. Reachability was checked against this app rather than assumed: there is no middleware.ts, no i18n config, no Server Actions ('use server' appears nowhere in src/), no rewrites in next.config.js, and no custom server. That rules out the i18n proxy bypass (GHSA-36qx-fr4f-26g5), both Server Actions issues (GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj, GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x), and the rewrite-destination SSRF (GHSA-p9j2-gv94-2wf4) on the current surface. The residual exposure is the RSC/WebSocket-upgrade DoS and SSRF cluster against a build that is 405 static paths with two dynamic routes.
exceptions.remediation: Requires next >= 15.5.21. Plan a Next 15 migration slice (App Router codemods, eslint-config-next bumped in lockstep, full test/lint/build/audit pass). Re-verify the reachability assumptions above if middleware, i18n, Server Actions, rewrites, or a custom server are ever introduced — any of those would invalidate this waiver early.

exceptions.reason: The direct devDependency was raised to ^8.5.26 and that top-level copy is fully patched. The two remaining highs (GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q and GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849, arbitrary .map file disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL) come from node_modules/next/node_modules/postcss only, which next@14.2.35 pins to exactly 8.4.31 in its own dependencies — it cannot be overridden without leaving Next 14. Build-time CSS processing over CSS authored in this repo; no untrusted stylesheet ever reaches it, and it is not present in the deployed bundle.
exceptions.remediation: Cleared by the same Next 15 migration as the `next` entry above, which unpins the bundled postcss.

exceptions.reason: Command injection in the glob CLI's -c/--cmd flag. Reached only as a transitive dev dependency of the lint toolchain; this repo never invokes the glob CLI, and no CI job passes -c/--cmd. Still present after the 14.2.35 bump — npm reports the only fix as eslint-config-next@16.3.1, a semver-major jump that would outpace the pinned Next 14 runtime. Not reachable at runtime or in the deployed bundle.
exceptions.approvedBy: P0-adapted slice, 2026-08-14; re-confirmed by the dependency-security slice, 2026-08-14, pending human confirmation
exceptions.remediation: Cleared by the eslint-config-next major bump that accompanies the Next 15 migration.
